page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of system memory, yielding a 4.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, ensuring dedicated CPU resources without hyperthreading. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 instruction cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% at 2692.58. However, multi-core performance is comparatively limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also a constraint, with read-only large block bandwidth at 35.65 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 22.54 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression demonstrate average performance, while multi-threaded decompression and database operations are weak.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC hardware profile and balanced resource allocation, the t2d-standard-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that require dedicated CPU execution without the overhead of shared-core resource contention. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, basic web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, and small-scale development or testing environments that do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-threaded compute capabilities.
